sources: Clean architecture dependency rule: dependencies point inward; the domain never imports infrastructure (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md in this case)
Python relative import semantics: a relative import resolves against the package of the importing module (concept; not web-verified in this run)

defects.class: layer direction violated: domain imports infrastructure through a relative import
defects.description: Quoted line 28: from ..infrastructure.repo import SqlRepo. The module is shop/domain/cart.py, so the leading two dots resolve to the package shop and the import reaches shop.infrastructure.repo. The rule in rules/ARCHITECTURE.md forbids the domain from importing infrastructure by absolute or relative import. The line is inside the Cart.price_of method, so the import is local to the method and does not appear at module top, which makes the layer breach easy to miss on a quick read. Resolving the target needs the package layout (shop/infrastructure/repo.py), which is why the defect is cross-file. Price lookup in the domain is coupled to the SQL adapter SqlRepo, so the domain cannot run without the infrastructure layer.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: from ..domain.cart import Cart. The application layer may import the domain, and the import resolves to shop.domain.cart, which is the allowed direction. Only the infrastructure target is forbidden in shop/domain/.

from ..domain.cart import Cart. Infrastructure may import the domain (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md, layer rule for infrastructure). The import resolves to shop.domain.cart, and the dependency points inward. Only the reverse direction, domain importing infrastructure, is a violation.
Preexisting module-level catalogue dict outside the hunk this diff adds; not part of the change.
